record.original_question: For each pattern length k, determine whether the largest Stanley-Wilf limit among all classical patterns of length k is always attained by a layered pattern.

evidence.quote: One of the weakest of these conjectures, widely believed to be true, is made explicit in [23, Conjecture 1] (although it may have been made before) and says that among all patterns of a given length k, the largest Stanley-Wilf limit is attained by some layered pattern.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A permutation $\pi \in S_n$ is said to *contain* a pattern $\tau \in S_k$ if there exist indices $1 \le i_1 < i_2 < \cdots < i_k \le n$ such that the subsequence $\pi(i_1), \pi(i_2), \ldots, \pi(i_k)$ is order-isomorphic to $\tau(1), \tau(2), \ldots, \tau(k)$; otherwise $\pi$ *avoids* $\tau$. Let $S_n(\tau)$ denote the number of permutations of $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ that avoid $\tau$. The Marcus–Tardos theorem (resolving the Stanley–Wilf conjecture) implies that the limit
$$L(\tau) := \lim_{n\to\infty} S_n(\tau)^{1/n}$$
exists and is finite for every pattern $\tau$.

A permutation $\tau \in S_k$ is called *layered* if it is a concatenation of contiguous blocks (layers) such that within each block the entries are decreasing, and the blocks themselves are arranged so that all entries of an earlier block are smaller than all entries of any later block. Equivalently, $\tau$ is layered if it can be written as a direct sum of decreasing permutations.

Question: Is it true that for every integer $k \ge 1$,
$$\max_{\tau \in S_k} L(\tau)$$
is attained by some layered permutation $\tau \in S_k$?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that, among all classical patterns of a given length, the maximum Stanley–Wilf limit is attained by a layered pattern remains open. It is supported by computational enumeration for small lengths and is discussed as a still-believed open conjecture in the recent literature on Stanley–Wilf limits and pattern 1324; partial results give upper bounds (e.g., $L(\tau) \le 4\ell^2$ for layered $\tau$ of length $\ell$), but no general proof or disproof is known.

status_evidence.title: Upper bounds for the Stanley-Wilf limit of 1324 and other layered patterns
status_evidence.snippet: Upper bounds for the Stanley-Wilf limit of layered patterns of length ℓ at most 4ℓ^2; conjecture about layered patterns achieving the maximum is referenced as open.
status_evidence.claim: Layered-pattern maximum conjecture treated as an open conjecture supported by partial upper bounds.

status_evidence.title: Stanley-Wilf limits are typically exponential (Fox)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses growth rates of Stanley-Wilf limits and the role of layered patterns in conjectured extremal behavior.
status_evidence.claim: The layered extremality conjecture is referenced as still-open.
